subject: Urban Planning
title: Indigenous Land Governance
description: A quick, practical guide to Indigenous Land Governance.

hook.text: Before colonial zoning, Indigenous peoples governed land through stewardship, not ownership. The land wasn't a commodity.

buildup.text: Fire management, seasonal rotation, and shared access maintained ecosystems for thousands of years.

discovery.text: Australian Aboriginal land management created the mosaic landscapes that European settlers mistook for 'wilderness.'

twist.text: Colonial land laws divided this managed landscape into private parcels. Stewardship was replaced by extraction.

climax.text: Land-back movements and co-management agreements are returning governance of some lands to Indigenous communities.

punchline.text: They managed this land for millennia. We could learn how.

quiz.question: How did Indigenous land governance differ from colonial zoning?
options: Indigenous peoples used strict private property boundaries enforced by tribal law
Land was managed through stewardship and shared access, not private ownership
Indigenous communities didn't interact with the land and left it entirely wild
